name: Sell-Through & Inventory Health core scenarios
description: Real Sell-Through & Inventory Health Q&A pairs grounded in the synthetic seed data (see data/generate_seed_data.py): weekly sell-through % by category, aging inventory 90+ days at risk, weeks of supply by store, and retail sell-through benchmarks. NOT currently wired to a runnable eval CLI gate: `adk eval` (google-adk 2.5.0) doesn't support YAML Agent Config agents (confirmed 2026-07-26 against ADK source, see architecture spec section 8) -- these cases are content-ready but need either a different eval mechanism or an ADK fix before they run as a quality gate.

parts.text: What was our weekly sell-through percentage by category for the week ending July 24, 2026?

For the week ending July 24, 2026, Men's Outerwear achieved a higher sell-through rate (~75-85%) across stores, while Women's Footwear averaged around 50-60%, based on internal weekly sell-through data.
Which products have significant inventory in the 90+ days aging bucket at risk of markdown?
Ankle Boots (SKU-005) and Sandals (SKU-006) have significant aging inventory in the 90+ days bucket flagged with markdown risk across multiple stores, based on internal aging inventory data.
How does weeks of supply compare across our stores?

STORE-001 has the lowest weeks of supply (around 3 to 4 weeks, indicating fast stock turn), whereas STORE-003 has the highest weeks of supply (around 8 to 10 weeks, indicating overstocking), based on internal store inventory and sell-through data.
What are the typical retail industry sell-through benchmarks for seasonal apparel and footwear?

Typical retail industry benchmarks for seasonal apparel sell-through range from 65% to 80% at full price before initial markdowns, while footwear typically targets 60% to 75% full-price sell-through per season, based on external market data.
